 HAMILTON COUNTY, Tenn. — Tennessee drivers will face a new requirement when registering a vehicle for the first time beginning in January. 
 Hamilton County Clerk Office is reminding motorists to bring proof of citizenship or lawful presence to avoid delays when registering their vehicles.
 According to a news release from the Hamilton County Clerk's Office, the new requirement stems from legislation passed by the Tennessee General Assembly earlier this year.
 Under Tennessee Code Annotated Section 55-4-144, anyone applying for an initial vehicle registration that includes issuing a license plate must provide documentation establishing U.S. citizenship, lawful permanent residency or federally authorized temporary presence in the country. 
 Acceptable documentation includes a REAL ID-compliant license, Tennessee driver's license or Tennessee photo identification card, along with other documents approved by the state. 
 The requirement applies statewide and will be handled locally by county clerk offices. 
 Annual vehicle registration renewals will not be affected by the new documentation requirement. 
 Weaver is encouraging motorists to review the requirements and gather necessary paperwork before visiting the clerk's office to avoid delays. 
 The Tennessee Department of Revenue has published a list of acceptable documents and identification on its website. 
 The new requirements take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
